relationships.contract: ResourceRef + logicalTime -> effective ResourceScopeAffiliation[] with validity/provenance
effective Policy Rules with governed subject/provenance
applicable ComponentPlacements / ResourceRefs with resolution state
ResourceRef + logicalTime -> effective AddressSpace[0..1] = HostAddress | Prefix with resolution/provenance
MVP: HostAddress TrafficPair -> FirewallCandidate[] -> accessListNames[]; Prefix input unresolved until edge is widened
TargetRequiredPolicy[] by comparisonScope firewallId + accessListName, or unresolved
provider-native configured policy for explicit comparison scope
MVP VerifiedChangeIntent(ENSURE-PERMIT missingPermitSpace) + target/provider capability + base configured/target correlation
TargetPolicyArtifact with target/comparison scope, base correlation, artifact digest, renderer identity/version, semantic-equivalence evidence and intent provenance

invariants: ACC owns Application/Component/Interaction semantics and not deployment placement.
Application Deployment owns logical deployment identity and Component-to-Resource placement truth.
Resource Catalogue owns Resource identity/lifecycle, scope affiliation/responsibility and effective AddressSpace.
For current scope one Resource has at most one effective AddressSpace at one logical time, represented as HostAddress or Prefix.
Application Deployment references ResourceRef only and owns no endpoint/address selection.
Resource address changes do not redefine Resource, ApplicationDeployment or GovernedInteractionSubject identity.
GovernedInteractionSubject identity is InteractionContractRevisionRef + source/destination ApplicationDeploymentRef.
Access Governance MVP requires exactly one distinct applicable Responsibility Scope per governance side; zero or several fail closed.
A material approval-obligation change withdraws current authorization without changing governed-subject identity.
Historical Access Requests/approvals cannot silently restore withdrawn current authorization.
Required Policy Materialization is derived composition; unresolved is not empty required policy or APR drift.
The first MVP NEP edge accepts only HostAddress-to-HostAddress TrafficPairs; Prefix remains upstream truth and yields unresolved materialization until Prefix-aware NEP semantics are accepted.
APR compares complete required/configured effective permit semantics by comparisonScope firewallId + accessListName using exact common/missing/excess algebra.
MVP remediation is additive-only: missing may produce ENSURE-PERMIT VerifiedChangeIntent; excess is report/audit evidence and not automatic removal authority.
Provider rendering must preserve verified semantic intent and fail closed when equivalence cannot be established.
NEO owns controlled execution and may not reinterpret APR intent or rendered artifact semantics.
Applied or immediate execution Verified is not final semantic convergence proof.
No Shared Kernel is accepted between target Bounded Contexts.
tactical_open_questions: Exact ApplicationDeployment lifecycle/status vocabulary and move-versus-replacement mechanics.
Whether multiple access-domain placements of the same Component on the same Resource require distinct identity.
Persistence/history migration from earlier ResourceEndpoint/EndpointAddress representation to Resource-level AddressSpace without losing provenance.
Broader APR technical-region/change-design/scale semantics beyond the first additive MVP slice.
explicit_future_extensions: Generalized Access Governance approval semantics when several Responsibility Scopes apply to one side.
Prefix-aware NEP TrafficPair routing/override matching semantics without host enumeration.
Managed-policy ownership and automatic removal/narrowing semantics for APR excess.
Richer APR remediation vocabulary beyond additive ENSURE-PERMIT.
Multiple simultaneous Resource addresses/prefixes, interfaces, endpoint purpose, VIP and deployment-specific network exposure require a future confirmed use case and affected-edge reopen.
Production provider transport, generic rollback and multi-target transaction semantics.
